newsitem.title: THAILAND: New Thai finmin Thanong to seek Amnuay's advice.
newsitem.headline: New Thai finmin Thanong to seek Amnuay's advice.

text.p: Thailand's new finance minister Thanong Bidaya said on Saturday he would meet Amnuay Viravan, the man he replaced, to seek his advice on policies to bail the country out of its current economic crisis.
"I plan to meet my predecessor Dr Amnuay and seek his advice," he told a local television station.
Thanong was appointed on Friday, a day after Amnuay quit abruptly following disagreements with his political rivals in the coalition government of premier Chavalit Yongchaiyudh.

Thanong pledged at a news conference on Friday that he would pursue Amnuay's fiscal and monetary policies, saying they were mostly on the right track in tackling Thailand's worst economic slump in over a decade.
Chavalit has said the same thing.
Thailand's economy is growing at its most sluggish level for 10 years, with private forecasts predicting a slowdown to between three and five percent versus 6.4 percent in 1996.
The economy has yet to recover from a confidence crisis in its finance sector.
Thanong is a low profile banker and was chief executive of Thai Military Bank Plc.

Amnuay's resignation triggered renewed speculation that Thailand may alter its foreign exchange regime by either devaluing its baht or by widening the spread within which the baht is allowed to fluctuate against other currencies.

The new finance minister has declined to commit himself to any change in baht policy or comment on whether a change is likely in Thailand's high interest rates, which the government maintains to discourage capital outflows.

He has also declined so far to spell out what he plans to do to rescue Thailand's battered finance companies, which face a crisis of confidence and acute liquidity problems from their over-exposure to the property sector.
